File surface: **set by the premise measurement, before any code.** The os-dev first measures on origin/main (after #34965, `3a78b898`) and stops before design. The area then restates this claim with the measured surface and the serial-constraint scan. The two routes the card allows:
- (a) a one-off normalisation step: the repo's existing upgrade or migration mechanism for the SQL driver (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/**` and whatever runner owns upgrade steps). It rewrites text-stored booleans (`'true'`/`'false'`, and `'1'`/`'0'` if measured) to the driver's boolean form, per object and per boolean field, idempotently;
- (b) a read-side fix: equality filters on a boolean field match both the stored boolean and its text forms, if the measurement shows that is cheap and index-safe.
Pins go beside the edited files (a row seeded with the text `'false'` is found by `= false` after the step or with the read fix), plus a root `.changeset/`.

Reversibility and dry run (route a, stated before any build at the seat's order):
- **Reversibility.** The rewrite maps each canonical text reading to exactly one boolean (`'true'`→true, `'false'`→false) and leaves every other value untouched. The forward map is lossless in meaning but forgets which rows were text. The step therefore records, per object and field, the ids it rewrote and the original text, in its report or log, so an operator can restore them. A down step is offered only if the repo's migration mechanism has one. A non-canonical text value (anything outside the measured readings) is never rewritten; it is counted and reported.
- **Dry run.** The step has a read-only mode that counts candidate rows per object and field and writes nothing. The real run is the same query plus the update, in one transaction per object where the driver allows it. A second run rewrites 0 rows (idempotent), and the pin proves it.
- **Where it runs.** Not at boot by default unless the repo's upgrade convention says so. The premise names the mechanism and how an operator invokes it.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: TIER_DEFAULT (re-derived at the restated claim)`, `effort: high` (seat order)
Clause-②: no (provisional, restated with the surface): route (a) rewrites stored values to the form new writes already take since #34965, and no accepted input or answer narrows. Route (b) widens what a boolean equality filter matches; it is restated as `yes (widening …)` and sent to seat L2 if chosen.
Metadata-protocol: none (provisional; restated if the step needs a manifest or upgrade-protocol entry)
Responsibility: `boolean fields on the SQL driver (objectstack): rows written by the inline grid before #34965 still hold the text 'true'/'false', so equality filters (won = false) and requiredWhen over queries miss them until each row is re-saved | #34965 fixed new writes and the read of a stored 'false'/'0', not the stored data | every app on the SQL driver that edited booleans in a master-detail inline grid before 18.5.x-next`
Thread-read: 6961931895
Premise: to be measured on origin/main first: (1) which text readings exist in stored rows and how the filter compiles them; (2) the repo's upgrade or migration mechanism and its dry-run and down conventions; (3) the cost of a read-side match (index use, the SQLite and Postgres dialects).
Serial constraints cleared: `deferred to the restated claim (the surface is not known yet); the dev runs overlap-check on its probe push`
Pre-claim lane: `domain:server`

Prior rulings read: seat ruling 6957305509 (backfill ruled out of #34965), L1-d 6959775843 → read; migration / upgrade-step rulings → read at the restated claim

repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzg2evNa1V3zxrQq3KX

Claim amendment: area o3-A · 2026-11-17T22:57Z · restates claim 6963136422 after the premise report 6963386869 and the seat's ruling (relayed to the area at 22:57Z). It supersedes the provisional lines.

## Premise (measured on origin/main `4443014630c`, wider than filed)
- Only SQLite can hold text booleans, and only as `'true'` / `'false'` (NUMERIC affinity). Postgres, MSSQL, MySQL and Oracle coerce or refuse the text (code reading; no rig).
- On those rows, `=`, `$in`, `!=` and `$nin` all answer wrongly, at the driver, the engine and the REST door. ORDER BY sorts them after every integer. Aggregate groupBy presents a text `'false'` as true (`presentReadValue`, `sql-driver-filter-helpers.ts:333`). `requiredWhen` is unaffected since #34965.
- The engine cannot address these rows: a read presents them as booleans, and a `'false'` comparand narrows to false. So the fix is raw SQL in the driver.

## Seat ruling (22:57Z), quoted
> route (a) is approved. backfillCanonicalBooleans becomes the fourth driver storage convergence, beside the datetime, time and JSON backfills: one guarded idempotent UPDATE per column, normalize_boolean_storage previewed under deferred DDL, non-canonical text withheld and warned. (1) Record: follow the convention, a count plus a capped id sample with no down step. Your reason holds, since an undo would only restore the broken form.

## Route (a): file surface
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`: `backfillCanonicalBooleans`, and `previewBooleanConvergence` called from `previewDeferredSchemaWork`.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-rotation.ts`: one call beside the datetime, time and JSON backfills (~:661-666), plus the host `Pick`.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`: host stubs, if the rotation host needs them.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts`: a new `PendingSchemaWorkKind` value, `normalize_boolean_storage`. It counts as in place under the existing `isInPlaceSchemaWork` rule, and the CLI renderer is generic, so no CLI file changes.
- New pins beside these files, and a root `.changeset/` (driver-sql).
- If the docs page `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, which lists `normalize_datetime_storage`, needs the new kind, one line there.

## Record and reversibility (amended to the ruling)
The claim promised per-row ids and the original text. It now follows the convergence convention: an info log line per table and field with the rows converted and a capped sample of ids. There is no down step. The rewrite keeps meaning (since #34965 a text row reads the same as its integer), so an undo would only restore the defective form. The dry run is `os migrate plan` under deferred DDL, which counts the rows as `normalize_boolean_storage`. `os migrate apply` runs it after confirmation. An ordinary boot runs it automatically, unless `OS_SKIP_SCHEMA_SYNC=1`. Non-canonical text is never rewritten; it is counted and warned about. Each column is one atomic UPDATE.

## Pins the seat will look for
A second boot changes 0 rows. `=`, `$in`, `!=` and `$nin`, ORDER BY and groupBy over a mixed column, before and after. The `OS_SKIP_SCHEMA_SYNC` skip. The non-canonical warn path. The deferred-DDL preview count.

Clause-②: yes (widening: `@objectstack/driver-sql` exports `PendingSchemaWorkKind` from its index, and the CLI consumes it, so the union gains one published value, `normalize_boolean_storage`; boolean filters, sorts and groupBy on SQLite now answer legacy text rows as their boolean)
Metadata-protocol: none (no spec file is touched)
Container & model: `S/M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: TIER_DEFAULT`, `effort: high`. Review: L1-d, then seat L2 (writes stored rows at every boot; fable on the driver contract per the Clause-② line).
Serial constraints cleared: at the premise, no open PR touched `packages/drivers/driver-sql/` or the CLI migrate files; the dev re-runs overlap-check on the first push.
